title: Add your microphone
summary: Pick the right microphone in Settings, Audio and check it in the Audio Mixer.

steps.say: Click Settings in the Controls panel at the bottom right.
hints: Settings is the second button from the bottom of the Controls panel, above Exit.
You can also open the File menu and choose Settings.
steps.why: The global microphone is chosen in Settings so it works in every scene.

steps.say: Click Audio in the list on the left side of Settings.

checks.prompt: Is the Audio page of OBS Settings showing, with Global Audio Devices?

hints: Audio sits between Output and Video in the left list.
Use the Down arrow key in the left list until Audio is selected.
steps.why: The Audio page holds the device choices for Desktop Audio and Mic/Aux.

steps.say: Under Global Audio Devices, set Mic/Auxiliary Audio to your microphone.

checks.prompt: Is the Mic/Auxiliary Audio dropdown set to a named device instead of Disabled?

hints: Default uses whatever Windows treats as the main microphone; picking it by name is more reliable.
If your microphone is missing, check it is plugged in and allowed under Windows microphone privacy settings.
steps.why: Choosing the device by name stops OBS switching mics when Windows changes its default.

steps.say: Click OK at the bottom right of Settings to save and close.
hints: Apply saves without closing; OK saves and closes.
steps.why: OBS only uses new settings after OK or Apply.

steps.say: Say a few words out loud and watch the Mic/Aux meter in the Audio Mixer. Say done when it moves.

checks.prompt: In the Audio Mixer, does the Mic/Aux meter show a green or yellow level bar?

hints: If the meter is still, check the speaker icon beside Mic/Aux is not crossed out.
Aim for speech peaking in the yellow part; red means it is too loud.
steps.why: A moving meter proves OBS hears you before you record anything long.
